To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sensitivity of NMR-based screening experiments for the detection of ligand–DNA binding can be significantly improved by the use of paramagnetic tags, and that the use of different paramagnetic ions can be exploited to optimize the detection of different types of ligand–nucleic acid interactions.

(i) a paramagnetic center can be placed in a DNA oligonucleotide, (ii) the presence of the metal ion in the macromolecule increases the sensitivity of the screening, (iii) different metal ions can be used to modulate the effect of the paramagnetic probe, and (iv) this strategy permits the identification of weak ligands for the target DNA.
the sensitivity of a NMR screening strategy can be improved by using short oligonucleotids functionalized with paramagnetic metal ions.

the use of NMR spectroscopy to characterize DNA–drug interactions and with the development of new strategies for drug screening.

the development of a strategy for the identification and characterization of weak interactions between ligands and nucleic acids, based on NMR spectroscopy, which can be applied to a wide range of ligands and targets, and is particularly suitable for the screening of large libraries of chemicals.
the use of paramagnetic probes in NMR experiments to increase the sensitivity of ligand screening experiments.

the use of a paramagnetic center inserted into the target molecule can significantly improve the sensitivity in the detection of ligand–macromolecule interaction by means of NMR experiments, and can be used to detect weak binders.
the insertion of a paramagnetically tagged nucleic acid target, in combination with a CPMG-edited NMR approach, can be successfully used for screening purposes, to identify weak binders.

we were able to show how the sensitivity of the screening method based on the recording CPMG spectra of ligands in the presence of a DNA target, can be increased by the insertion of a paramagnet in the DNA.
we were able to demonstrate the possibility to use the insertion of a paramagnet to increase sensitivity in the detection of ligand–DNA interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sensitivity of the R2-edited NMR method is increased by a factor of 10 when a paramagnetic probe is placed in the macromolecular target.
the insertion of a paramagnet in a DNA target increases the sensitivity of R2-edited NMR experiments, and allows the identification of weak ligand–DNA binders.

, in the case of a target with low molecular weight, such as DNA, the insertion of a paramagnet in the target is a very efficient strategy to enhance sensitivity, and to increase the chances of detecting weak interactions.
